threads.thread_goal: Align on current customer journey and main pain points across channels.

messages.text:
Kicking off this thread to map how customers move across our channels today for the Cross-Channel Customer Experience Upgrade for Retail Network.

For T1 we need a simple journey view and the main pain points. From the contact centre side, a typical path I see is:
- Customer calls after seeing something in store or in a leaflet
- We check stock or policy, sometimes call the store or account manager
- We log the issue in our own notes, but it is not yet aligned with the shared A5 log

Biggest issues I notice:
1) Customers repeat their story when moving between store, phone, and field visits
2) Inconsistent answers on refunds and complaints
3) Slow follow-up when something needs a field visit

Can each of you describe the main steps and pain points you see in your part of the journey so we can stitch together a first version for T1

From the account management side, a common journey is:
- Customer visits store, gets basic info
- They are referred to me for a more complex quote or contract
- I schedule a visit, then follow up later by phone or email

Pain points I see:
- I often do not get full context from the store about what was already promised
- After my visit, if the customer calls the contact centre, they sometimes get a different explanation on timelines or conditions
- I track follow-ups in my own notes, not yet in A5, so others cannot see the history

For T1 I can sketch a simple journey diagram that shows where store, contact centre, and field visits connect. I will draft something and share back here.

Adding to what 49060 shared, on my accounts I see a lot of back and forth like this:
- Customer sees a promotion in store
- They ask the store team for a better deal for their company
- Store gives my contact, I step in later

The tricky parts:
- I do not always know which promotion rules the store used
- When I call back, the customer expects the same conditions they heard in store, but sometimes that is not possible

I am not fully sure how to represent this in the journey map for T1. Maybe we can have a separate lane for promotions and discounts so we do not miss it

From the specialised seller view in store, a typical path is:
- Customer walks in, looks around
- We greet them and ask what they are looking for
- If it is a simple purchase, we close it on the spot
- If it is more complex, we either call the contact centre or pass the lead to an account manager

Pain points I see:
- We do not have a clear rule on when to involve the contact centre versus an account manager
- When customers come back with a complaint, they sometimes say the phone team told them something different
- I do not have an easy way to log these cases into A5 yet, so they stay in my notebook

For T1, I can list the main in-store touchpoints and where we hand over to other channels.

On the food service side inside the store, the journey is usually:
- Customer comes to the counter after walking through the store
- They ask about products, ingredients, or combos
- We serve them and sometimes they ask about wider store offers or loyalty

Pain points:
- During busy times, we cannot always give full explanations, so customers are told to call later or ask at the main till
- If there is a complaint about food quality or cleanliness, I am not sure how that should be logged in A5 so others can see it

For T1 I can map the steps from when they approach the counter to when they leave, and where we redirect them to contact centre or account manager.

From my side in crop production, I mostly see customers when they have questions about specific products or orders that were placed earlier.

Typical path:
- They may have ordered through the store or by phone
- They come to check on delivery or product condition
- If something is wrong, I try to solve it or send them back to the store desk

Pain points:
- I am not always sure what the store or contact centre promised before
- I do not know exactly which fields in A5 I should fill when I hear a complaint, so sometimes I just tell the store team verbally

For T1 I can list the main steps I see and where I think we should capture feedback more clearly.

Thanks all, this is already giving us a good picture for T1.

I will start drafting a simple journey map with these stages:
1) Discover: customer sees promotion or visits store
2) Explore: they talk to store or food service staff, maybe get referred to contact centre
3) Decide: they speak with an account manager if needed
4) Use: they receive the product or service
5) Post-purchase: they contact us again for questions, refunds, or complaints

Can you confirm if these five stages cover your reality, or if we need to split any of them

Those five stages work for me. For account management, the Decide and Post-purchase stages are where most of my work sits.

Maybe in the Post-purchase stage we can explicitly mention that customers might switch channels: they might call, visit the store, or ask me directly. That is where the inconsistent answers show up.

For T1 I can add a note under Post-purchase about cross-channel contact so we remember to address it later in the playbook.

Agree with the five stages. I would just highlight that promotions can start in Discover but also appear again in Post-purchase when customers ask for better conditions after they already bought.

Maybe we can mark promotions as a recurring element across stages in the T1 diagram, so we remember to align rules later.

From the store floor, the five stages make sense. I like that Discover and Explore are separate, because sometimes customers just browse and only later ask for help.

In Explore, could we note that we should always check if the customer already contacted the call centre or an account manager before, so we do not restart from zero That might reduce the repeating-the-story issue.

I am also fine with the five stages. For food service, most of the interaction is in Explore and Use.

In Post-purchase, when someone complains about food or cleanliness, I think we should have a clear step to log it in A5 instead of just solving it on the spot and forgetting it. That would help us see patterns.

The stages look ok to me too. I mostly see Use and Post-purchase.

I like the idea of having a clear step to log issues in A5. I will need some guidance on which fields to fill, but that can come later when we define the reporting routine.

Great, sounds like we have alignment on the five-stage journey for T1.

Now, to narrow down the main pain points we will prioritise in the playbook, here is what I heard so far:
1) Customers repeating their story when they move between channels
2) Inconsistent answers on refunds, complaints, and promotions
3) Lack of visibility on previous promises or follow-ups between store, contact centre, and account managers
4) Slow or unclear follow-up after field visits or complex cases

Are these the right four to focus on, or is there anything more critical we are missing

Those four cover most of what I see. If we address them, my visits and follow-ups will be much smoother.

Maybe we can include under point 4 that responsibilities for follow-up are not always clear. That way, when we design the field visit guide and reporting, we can assign who does what.

I agree with the four pain points. The only thing I would add is that sometimes we do not capture compliments or positive feedback in A5, only complaints. That makes it harder to see what is working.

Not sure if that should be a top pain point now or something we handle later when we define metrics.

From the store side, I am ok with those four. The repeating-the-story and inconsistent answers are the ones customers complain about the most.

I would keep the positive feedback point in mind, but I do not think it needs to be in the top four right now.

Same here. Those four pain points match what I hear at the counter.

If we can make it easier to log issues in A5 and have clear rules for refunds and complaints, that will already be a big improvement.

I am fine with those four as well. For me the biggest one is not knowing what others promised before.

Happy to go ahead with that list.

Thanks all. Let us lock in the journey and the four priority pain points so we can move on.

Decision D1: We will prioritise these four pain points in the playbook:
1) Customers repeating their story across channels
2) Inconsistent answers on refunds, complaints, and promotions
3) Lack of visibility on previous promises and follow-ups
4) Slow or unclear follow-up ownership on complex cases

Decision D2: For T1 we will use the five-stage journey (Discover, Explore, Decide, Use, Post-purchase) with cross-channel contact and promotions noted as recurring elements.

I will update the T1 journey draft and link it to A5 so we can start capturing examples against these stages.

threads.thread_goal: Define the structure and core behaviours of the unified playbook.

messages.text:
As a follow-up to the journey work in T1, I have drafted an outline for the Unified Customer Experience Playbook in A1 for T2.

Proposed structure:
1) Introduction and principles
2) Common behaviours across all channels
3) Store and food service guidelines
4) Contact centre call flow (linked to A3 and T4)
5) Field sales and account management visits (linked to A4 and T5)
6) Refunds, complaints, and cross-channel policy
7) Customer feedback and reporting using A5

For section 2, I suggest we pick 3–5 behaviours that must be the same everywhere. Initial ideas:
- Consistent greeting and closing
- Checking for previous interactions
- Clear explanation of next steps and ownership

Please review this outline and suggest changes before we lock it for T2.

Thanks for sharing the A1 outline.

From the account management side, I like that field visits (A4, T5) and refunds/complaints are separate sections. That will help me explain things consistently.

For the common behaviours, I would add:
- Confirming understanding by summarising what the customer said
- Recording key points in A5 or our local notes so others can see the history later

I am ok with the overall structure, but I wonder if we should merge the store and food service guidelines into one section with sub-parts, so it is shorter to navigate.

Looking at the outline, I like that we have a dedicated section for metrics and reporting using A5.

For field visits in A4 and T5, could we include a short checklist for what to capture after each visit, like commitments, deadlines, and who owns the next step That would help with the follow-up pain point we identified.

From the store floor, the structure looks clear. I agree with 49060 that store and food service could be in one section with sub-headings, so staff can find what they need quickly.

For the common behaviours, I would suggest we include:
- Using simple language, avoiding internal terms
- Always checking if the customer has already contacted another channel

That would help with the repeating-the-story issue.

I like the outline in A1. For food service, having our part under the store section with a clear sub-heading works for me.

For the 3–5 common behaviours, I would add one more:
- Keeping the environment and presentation clean and welcoming, since that affects the experience even before we speak.

We can then have more detailed cleanliness steps in the store section and in the checklist later.

From my side, the outline seems ok, but I have a small doubt.

In the reporting section with A5, will we have examples of how to fill the sheet for different situations For example, a complaint about product quality versus a compliment about service. That would help me know what to write.

Good point on examples for A5. Yes, in the reporting section we can add 3–4 short examples showing how to fill the sheet for a complaint, a compliment, and a suggestion.

On the structure, I hear a few themes:
- Keep store and food service together with sub-headings
- Make sure field visits include a follow-up checklist (A4, T5)
- Add a clear common behaviours section with 3–5 items

Before we finalise, does anyone see a missing section or something that should be removed to keep the playbook short enough for frontline use

I do not see anything major missing. Maybe we can keep the introduction very short, like half a page, so people can jump quickly to the behaviours and channel sections.

For the common behaviours, I would propose this list to react to:
1) Warm greeting and clear closing
2) Check for previous interactions and promises
3) Summarise the request to confirm understanding
4) Explain next steps, timing, and who owns them
5) Capture key points in A5 or local notes

That is five items, but they are all important for the pain points we chose.

I like that list. Maybe we can fold the environment cleanliness point from 45990 into the store section instead of the common behaviours, so the cross-channel list stays focused on conversation steps.

With that tweak, I am comfortable using these five as our shared behaviours.

Works for me. The five behaviours are easy to remember and match what we already try to do, just more consistently.

I agree that cleanliness can be detailed in the store section and in the checklist, not in the cross-channel list.

I am ok with keeping the five common behaviours focused on the conversation.

We can highlight cleanliness and presentation in the store section and in the checklist work later, so it still gets attention.
The five behaviours look clear to me. Having the step to check for previous interactions will help a lot when customers come to me after already talking to someone else.

Thanks for all the input.

Decision D3: We will use the A1 structure you reviewed, with store and food service combined into one section with sub-headings, a short introduction, a dedicated common behaviours section, and separate sections for contact centre (A3, T4), field visits (A4, T5), refunds/complaints, and reporting with A5.

Decision D4: Our 3–5 common behaviours across all channels will be:
1) Warm greeting and clear closing
2) Check for previous interactions and promises
3) Summarise the request to confirm understanding
4) Explain next steps, timing, and ownership
5) Capture key points in A5 or local notes

I will update A1 under T2 with this structure and list so we can move on to the detailed channel guidelines.

threads.thread_goal: Agree on in-store checklist, refunds policy, and job aids content.

messages.text:
I have put together a first draft of the In-Store Merchandising and Cleanliness Checklist in A2 for T3, based on our store routines.

The checklist is grouped into three areas and can be done in under 5 minutes:
1) Displays and product presentation
2) Stock levels and rotation
3) Cleanliness zones (entrance, counters, seating, restrooms if applicable)

I also started a list of ideas for the frontline job aid cards in A7 for T8, focusing on 3–5 key behaviours for store and food service.

Can you review and tell me what is missing or too detailed, especially thinking about busy times

Thanks for drafting A2.

From the store floor, the three areas make sense. A couple of thoughts:
- On displays, could we add a quick check that promotional materials match the current offers, so we do not advertise expired deals
- On cleanliness, maybe we can have a simple morning and mid-shift tick box, so it is clear when it was last checked

For the job aid cards in A7, I like the idea of having the 3–5 common behaviours on one side and a short reminder about refunds and complaints on the other.

Looking at A2 from my perspective, I wonder if we should include a quick check for products that come from crop production, like making sure they are stored correctly and not blocking exits.

I am not sure how detailed it should be, but maybe one line under stock levels would be enough.

From the contact centre side, A2 looks good and focused.

On the refunds and complaints policy in A6 for T6, I have drafted some wording to align store and contact centre procedures. It includes:
- Common rules on time limits and proof of purchase
- When store staff can decide on the spot
- When to escalate to the contact centre or an account manager

I would like store and specialised seller feedback on whether the examples in A6 feel realistic and easy to apply at the till.

I reviewed A6. The structure is clear, but I have a concern about one example.

There is a case where the guideline says we should always send the customer to the contact centre for a refund above a certain amount. In practice, if the customer is in front of us and it is a clear case, sending them away can create frustration.

Could we adjust the example so that store managers have some room to decide on the spot within a defined range, and only send the more complex cases to the contact centre

Good points.

I will update A2 to add:
- A line under displays to check that promotions and price labels match current offers
- A simple morning and mid-shift tick box for cleanliness checks
- A note under stock levels about safe storage for crop-related products, as 24573 suggested

For A7, I like the idea of having the common behaviours on one side and a short refunds and complaints reminder on the other, aligned with A6.

On A6, from the account management side, I support what 200631 said.

Maybe we can define three bands:
- Small refunds: store can decide on the spot within clear rules
- Medium: store calls the contact centre for confirmation
- Large or complex: escalate to account manager

We can add one example for each band in A6 so it is easy to follow.

I agree with the three bands idea for A6.

Could we also include a short note on how to log refunds and complaints in A5, so that when a case reaches me I can see the history and not ask the customer to repeat everything

Thanks for adding the safe storage note to A2.

On A7, would it be possible to include a tiny reminder about where the A5 sheet is kept in the store For example, a line saying: log issues on the feedback sheet at the service desk. That would help me remember to use it when I am in the store area.

Thanks for the feedback on A6.

I will rework the refund and complaint rules in T6 to:
- Introduce the three bands that 49060 suggested
- Give store managers clear authority for small refunds
- Clarify when to call the contact centre and when to involve an account manager
- Add a short note on logging each case in A5, as 394531 requested

Once updated, I will flag it here for a quick final check before we sign off.

Yes, I can add that to A7.

I will include a small line on the card: log issues on the feedback sheet at the service desk (A5), so everyone knows where to go.

I will also make sure the job aid cards for T8 stay very visual, with icons for the 3–5 behaviours and a simple reminder about refunds and complaints aligned with A6.

After the updates 45990 mentioned, A2 looks practical to me. I can see myself using it quickly at the start of the shift.

For A7, having the common behaviours and a short refunds reminder will be very helpful at the till.

I reviewed the updated A6 draft.

The three bands and examples are clear, and the note about logging in A5 is helpful. From my side, this wording will make it easier to explain decisions to customers and keep consistency between store, contact centre, and field.

I am comfortable moving forward with this version.

Same here. The updated A6 covers the main situations I see, and the logging step in A5 will help me pick up cases without asking customers to repeat everything.

Happy to go ahead with this wording.

Thanks everyone for the reviews.

Decision D5: We sign off on the updated A2 merchandising and cleanliness checklist for T3, with the three areas, promotion checks, safe storage note, and simple timing boxes.

Decision D6: We approve the updated wording in A6 for T6, with the three refund bands, clear store and contact centre roles, escalation to account managers when needed, and the requirement to log cases in A5.

We will now use A2 and A6 as the basis for the in-store section of the playbook and for the job aid cards in A7 under T8.

threads.thread_goal: Plan pilot, training sessions, and feedback collection approach.

messages.text:
Now that we have the main pieces of the playbook in A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, and A7, we need to plan the pilot, training, and feedback collection.

Proposal:
- Pilot scope (T11): 1 store with food service, 1 store without food service, and 2 key accounts for field visits
- Training (T9): short 30–40 minute sessions per role, staying within the 2-hour limit overall
- Reporting (T7, T10): use A5 for daily feedback and A8 for a simple weekly CX metrics report

For the contact centre, I will run a short session on the call flow in A3 and escalation rules. For field sales, we will use A4 to walk through the visit script and follow-up.

Please share which locations or accounts you suggest for the pilot and any constraints on training times.

For the field side of the pilot (T11), I suggest we pick:
- One medium-size account that already has regular visits, so we can test A4 and the follow-up template without too much risk
- One newer account where we can try the full visit script from the start

On training (T9), I can run a 30-minute session with account managers to walk through A4 and how to log commitments and feedback into A5 and A8.

I am ok with those account choices for the pilot.

On training times, mornings are usually better for me before I go out on visits. Maybe we can schedule the field sales session early in the day.

For reporting, I will need some help setting up A8 for my accounts, as I am not very used to working with templates like that.

For the store pilot, I suggest we choose:
- One store with high traffic and food service, to test A2 and A7 under pressure
- One smaller store without food service, to see how the checklist works in a simpler setup

On training (T9), late afternoon works better for us, between peak times. A 30-minute session on the playbook highlights, A2, A6, and A7 should be enough if we keep it practical.

I agree with those store choices for T11.

For food service staff, we can do a short 20–30 minute session focused on:
- The key behaviours from A1
- How to use A2 quickly at the start of the shift
- Where to find A5 and how to log issues
- The job aid cards in A7

We can run it just before the afternoon rush so people can apply it right away.

For the pilot, I can join the high-traffic store with food service.

On training, I would benefit from a short session on how to fill A5 and how my notes feed into A8. Maybe 15–20 minutes is enough, as long as we have concrete examples.

For timing, mid-morning works best for me, between tasks.

For the contact centre part of the pilot, I propose we:
- Select a small group of agents to use the new call flow in A3 and the escalation rules linked to A6
- Run a 30-minute training (T9) to walk through A3, the common behaviours from A1, and how to log calls in A5

For reporting (T10), I suggest we track weekly:
- Number of complaints and compliments per channel
- Number of escalations between store, contact centre, and field
- A simple yes or no on whether the customer had to repeat their story

We can capture these in A8 as part of the pilot routine.

The proposed metrics for A8 make sense and link well to our pain points.

For the weekly reporting routine (T10), maybe we can:
- Have each role update their part of A8 once a week
- Do a short 15-minute review call or async summary to agree on any quick fixes

That should keep it light while still giving us a view of how the pilot is going.

I can handle updating A8 weekly for my pilot accounts if we keep the fields simple.

I like the idea of a short review, maybe at the end of the week, to see if we need to adjust anything in A4 or the follow-up process.

For the store training (T9), could we split it into two short huddles instead of one longer session For example, 20 minutes on the playbook and A2 one day, and 20 minutes on A6, A7, and A5 another day.

That might fit better around shifts and still stay within the 2-hour limit.

Splitting the store training into two huddles works for me.

We can do:
- Day 1: overview of A1, A2, and the common behaviours
- Day 2: focus on A6, A7, and how to log in A5

Each huddle 20–25 minutes, so we stay within the time limit and keep it practical.

For A7 and A5, during the pilot I can share one quick example per week of a case I logged, so we can see if the sheet is easy to use.

On the weekly review, I prefer an async summary in the channel, as it is sometimes hard for me to join calls.

Let me summarise the pilot proposal so far for T11:
- Stores: one high-traffic store with food service, one smaller store without food service
- Field: one medium-size existing account and one newer account
- Contact centre: a small group of agents using A3 and A6

Training (T9):
- Store and food service: two short huddles covering A1, A2, A6, A7, and A5
- Field sales: one 30-minute session on A4, A5, and A8
- Contact centre: one 30-minute session on A3, A1 behaviours, and A5

Reporting (T7, T10):
- Use A5 daily for feedback and issues
- Update A8 weekly with complaints, compliments, escalations, and repeat-story indicator
- Share a short weekly summary in this channel instead of a call

Is everyone ok with this setup, or do we need to adjust anything before we lock it in

The summary matches what we discussed. I am comfortable with the pilot accounts, training plan, and reporting routine.

From my side, no further changes needed.
I am ok with the plan as well. The timing and scope look manageable, and the weekly A8 update is clear.

The store pilot setup and training huddles work for me.

I like that we are using A5 and A7 actively during the pilot so we can see if they really help on the floor.
All good from my side. The huddle format will make it easier to fit training into shifts, and the high-traffic store will give us a good test of A2 and A7.
I am ok with the plan too. I will focus on using A5 during the pilot and sharing examples in this channel.

Thanks everyone.

Decision D7: We confirm the pilot locations and participants for T11 as summarised: one high-traffic store with food service, one smaller store without food service, two field accounts (one existing, one new), and a small group of contact centre agents.

Decision D8: We agree on the training schedule for T9 and the weekly reporting routine for T10, using A5 for daily feedback and A8 for weekly metrics, with a short async summary in this channel.

I will update the pilot and training plan in A1 and coordinate with local managers for scheduling. After the pilot, we will use T12 to finalise and sign off the playbook based on the feedback collected.
